question_record.context: A multi-stage security incident involving system recovery setting tampering was detected on host `vnevado-win11u`. A file `vssblatemp.exe` was observed being used to delete volume shadow copies on the system. This action might be an attempt by adversaries to prevent system recovery and deny access to backups. Multiple alerts have been flagged in relation to this incident, one of which involves a user account dropping ransomware-related files on several devices, and another indicating lateral movement to the jump server.
question_record.question: What is the name of the malware detected as active and running on the system?
solution: The user with SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522` was involved in tampering with system recovery settings.
A user account associated with IP address `99.83.111.100` was observed delivering ransomware-related files.
Lateral movement was carried out to the jump server identified by AadDeviceId `4d8d23e9-a77d-4e33-9435-b8c457e57ca1` using PSExec.
An active malware identified as `mimikatz.exe` was detected.

76.name: System recovery setting tampering
76.description:
System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]
•	bcdedit.exe can be used to disable automatic Windows recovery features by modifying boot configuration data using the following command: [bcdedit.exe /set default bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures & bcdedit /set default recoveryenabled no]

41.name: Possible compromised user account delivering ransomware-related files
41.description: A user account was observed dropping a ransomware-related file on several devices. An attacker may have compromised the said user account to move laterally across the network and infect as many devices with ransomware as possible. Automated remediation action may be taken to disable the account.

174.name: PSExec to Vnevado-jump
174.description: Lateral movement to the jump server

150.name: Active unknown malware was detected
150.description:
Malware and unwanted software are undesirable applications that perform annoying, disruptive, or harmful actions on affected machines. Some of these undesirable applications can replicate and spread from one machine to another. Others are able to receive commands from remote attackers and perform activities associated with cyber attacks.

A malware is considered active if it is found running on the machine or it already has persistence mechanisms in place. Active malware detections are assigned higher severity ratings.

Because this malware was active, take precautionary measures and check for residual signs of infection.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning
